title: A Train Journey
description: A young man takes a long train trip and meets an interesting stranger.
instructions: Read the text about a train journey, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: Last spring, Hugo travelled by train from Paris to Rome to visit his cousin. The journey took more than eleven hours. Hugo chose the train because he does not like flying. He also wanted to see the countryside from the window.

Hugo had a seat next to an older woman with a big red suitcase. Her name was Elena, and she was a painter. She showed Hugo some small paintings in her bag. They were pictures of mountains, lakes and small villages.

When the train went through the Alps, Elena took out her paints. She painted the snowy mountains very quickly. Hugo watched her and asked many questions. The hours passed fast, and he forgot to read his book.

Before Elena got off in Milan, she gave Hugo the painting of the mountains. Hugo was very surprised and thanked her many times. Today, the painting is on the wall of his bedroom. Every time he looks at it, he remembers that journey.

Hugo arrived in Rome late in the evening. His cousin Marco was waiting for him at the station with a big smile. Hugo was tired, but he could not stop talking about Elena and her paintings. Marco listened and laughed. 'You only wanted a quiet trip with your book!' he said.

Hugo stayed in Rome for one week. Every day, he and Marco walked around the old streets and visited famous places. One afternoon, Hugo bought a small notebook and some coloured pencils. He started to draw the buildings, the bridges and the fountains. His drawings were not as good as Elena's, but he enjoyed making them very much.

On the way home, Hugo took the train again. This time, he did not read his book either. He sat by the window and drew the hills, the farms and the rivers. A little girl in the next seat watched him and asked many questions. Hugo smiled, because he remembered his first journey with Elena. Before he got off in Paris, he gave the girl one of his drawings. She held it in both hands and said it was her best present ever.
